_comment: TEAM ROSTER — single source of truth for the /team skill. Edit this file to add/remove models or change who does what; the skill reads it fresh on every run and never hardcodes members. No skill edits needed. Shipped as the author's reference setup: Fable 5 orchestrating, Grok 4.5 (Grok Build CLI) auditing/verifying.

members.name: fable
members.notes: The orchestrating session itself — whatever model your session runs orchestrates (the reference setup runs Fable 5). Never delegated to. Owns all git, signing, release, and deploy operations, and the final report to the user.

members.name: grok-build
members.model: grok-composer-2.5-fast (default); pass -m grok-build for the heavier coder
strengths: independent verification (different model family, zero shared bias)
members.budget: grok-plan (SuperGrok / X Premium+ — does NOT consume Claude limits)
members.notes: Grok 4.5 via the Grok Build CLI, driven headless by the claude-grok-bridge wrapper (github.com/BlinkingSun/claude-grok-bridge). Setup: curl -fsSL https://x.ai/cli/install.sh | bash; grok login (SuperGrok or X Premium+ subscription), then install the bridge. If the wrapper is missing at run time, treat this member as disabled — audit/verify falls back to a different Claude model per the policies. Any other backend works too: point invoke at any CLI exposing the same interface (-c channels, -w worker mode, -d cwd, -f attach, text reply on stdout); see the README wrapper contract.

assignment._comment: role -> member name. Executor is tiered by task difficulty. If an assigned member is disabled or missing, fall back per the policies below.

policies: Every plan is audited by the plan_auditor (consult mode, read-only) before any executor starts. The audit must return: a verdict on the plan, an executor recommendation per subtask, and whether the plan should be split into independent pieces for parallel executors. The auditor advises; the orchestrator decides — but deviations from the audit are noted in the final report. Prefer an auditor from a different provider than the planner; if the assigned plan_auditor is disabled, fall back the same way as the verifier.

The verifier must be a different member than the executor of the task being verified. If the assigned verifier is disabled, use any enabled member from a different provider than the executor; as a last resort use a different Claude model than the one that wrote the code.
A member whose wrapper or CLI is not installed is treated as disabled — apply the same fallbacks, and tell the user which member was unavailable.
If an assigned executor tier is disabled, fall back: trivial -> default -> hard. Never silently upgrade to a heavier budget tier without noting it to the user.
Verifiers run in consult mode only (read-only). Executors run in worker mode only inside scratch dirs or git worktrees.
No member except the orchestrator may commit, push, sign, notarize, or deploy.
Never run any worker-mode member inside hardware-connected or release-critical directories (serial-connected equipment, device flashing, publish/deploy scripts).
Budget: prefer members whose budget field says they do not consume Claude limits for verification/research; reserve claude-plan (heavy) members for genuinely hard tasks.
Live team reports: relay each audit and verify result to the user as it lands — verdicts, contradictions, accepted vs rejected findings — not only in the final report.
